messages:
maya: Quick thread — thinking about probe/fallback semantics when CP can't reach customer endpoint in a VPC. We need a deterministic, low-noise approach. Thoughts?

eric: +1. Two high-level choices: rely on passive heartbeats (agent->CP) or have the CP do active probes (CP->agent). Passive is cheaper but masks asymmetric failures.

jess: We already have agent heartbeat every 30s. That tells liveness but not whether agent can reach model infra / relay. I think we need a lightweight traffic-like probe.

raj: What about a short TCP/TLS probe that reuses the agent mTLS identity and hits a dedicated probe endpoint (not user path)? E.g., HEAD /_probe. Minimal surface.

sylvia: Important: probes must be rate-limited and labeled so they don't touch billing or trigger downstream RL. Also audit-log probe auth.

eric: Implementation sketch: try CP->agent direct probe if controlplane path is up; if that fails, attempt regional relay path. If both fail, mark route degraded and switch routing policy.

maya: Proposed state machine (rough):
```
probe(seq):
  GET /_probe?seq=<n>  # use mTLS client cert, short timeout (500ms)
  if 200 -> route ok, record success_ts
  if 5xx/timeout -> retry with backoff (100ms, 500ms, 2s)
  after 3 failures -> state = DEGRADED
  while DEGRADED -> probe every 5s, cooldown 120s after success to avoid flapping
```

jess: Persist last-success timestamp and a cooldown flag per-tenant to avoid flip-flop during transient networking blips. Also expose a "force-clear" API for ops.

raj: Metrics we want: `probe_latency_ms`, `probe_failures_total`, `degraded_switches_total`, `degraded_duration_seconds`. Alert if degraded_switches_total > 5 for a single tenant in 1h.

sylvia: Security checklist: probes must be authenticated (mTLS + signed probe header), authorized by tenant ACL, and recorded in audit logs with probe_id. No user PII in probe payloads.

eric: Edge case: sticky KV caches / session affinity — if we flip to relay we must invalidate per-connection cache or attempt cache warm-up on relay to avoid correctness bugs. This is tricky for long-lived sessions.

jess: For write-heavy routes we can do graceful degradation: serve cached reads and return 429 for writes with explanatory header `X-Redwood-Fallback:relay` so clients can retry later.

eric: Rollout plan: behind feature flag + operator toggle. Canary on 5 tenants, monitor metrics + error budgets for 24h, then widen. Add unit/e2e synthetic tests that kill CP path and assert relay takeover.

maya: Action items: @eric prototype probe client & backoff, @jess design persistent cooldown store + ops API, @raj add metrics + alerts to grafana, @sylvia write probe security requirements, ops team to run canary. I'll draft a short RFC with state machine and rollout checklist.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-04-30 05:00 UTC :rocket:

maya: Thanks all — I'll drop the RFC link here when it's ready.
